text: Assimilation (linguistic). A process by which contiguous sounds in language tend to approximate or become alike. Thus hands becomes handz , the voiceless s assumes the voiced quality of d ; hemp from O. Eng. henep . The organs of speech, in passing from one mode of ARTICULATION (q.v.) to another, either carry forward somewhat of the position necessary for the former, or by anticipation draw back somewhat of the latter. ( B.I.W .)
